name: spot-multiword-places-across-two-words
_why: spec §3. The placement loop compared ONE token against the WHOLE term, so a multi-word term only ever landed when the engine happened to merge it into one token. cloud(5)/claudecode(10) = 0.60 and code(4)/claudecode(10) = 0.60 are both rejected at width 1; the width-2 window cloudcode(9)/claudecode(10) = 0.20 is what matches. Found by real dictation, and it was SILENT.

name: spot-multiword-window-ends-at-last-alphanumeric
_why: spec §3: the span ends at the last alphanumeric of the final word — the same boundary absorbTrailingDuplicates picks — so the sentence punctuation survives OUTSIDE the replaced range.
transcript: we shipped cloud code, then rested
expectText: we shipped Claude Code, then rested

name: spot-multiword-per-word-alignment-refuses-plausible-window
_why: spec §3: whole-window plausibility ALONE is a text-corrupting brake — load code measures 0.40 against Claude Code, inside the 0.45 ceiling. Per-word alignment (load↔Claude = 0.50) is what refuses it. Regression pin: the new width-2 machinery must not open this door.

name: spot-multiword-window-never-crosses-own-punctuation
_why: spec §3: cross plain spaces only, never a word's own punctuation. 'Claude,' + 'code' is not a window, so the width-2 scan must not fuse across the comma.

name: spot-multiword-already-correct-is-noop
_why: jot-shared#1, verbatim. applyFromDetections placed the two-word term onto the single token 'Claude' and the transcript's own 'code' survived after it → 'Claude Code code generated...'. decide step (2) waves every multi-word term through as precise and self-gating, so nothing downstream caught it. The width-2 window matches exactly here, so this is an identity no-op: unchanged text, and NO review row / UI chip.
transcript: Claude code generated most of the boiler plate
expectText: Claude code generated most of the boiler plate

name: spot-multiword-absorbs-trailing-duplicate
_why: spec §2: when the detection sits on the FIRST word only, the width-1 pick wins on proportional position and absorbTrailingDuplicates widens it onto the duplicated tail. Identity is then ORDINAL (not normalized) — the widening already proved the term's words are present, and casing IS the term for a multi-word proper noun — so the casing fix applies instead of being swallowed as a no-op.
transcript: Claude code generated most of the boiler plate
expectText: Claude Code generated most of the boiler plate

name: spot-multiword-host-token-punctuation-blocks
_why: spec §2, the sub-case Windows hit while implementing: the host token carries its OWN trailing punctuation. Widening eats the comma ('ask Claude Code review'); not widening publishes the duplicate ('ask Claude Code, code review'). Both mutate text on a guess → block and log.

name: spot-multiword-does-not-eat-a-real-following-word
_why: absorb at most (term words − span words): a span that already covers every term word absorbs NOTHING, so a genuine following 'code' survives.
transcript: I love cloud code code review
expectText: I love Claude Code code review

name: spot-possessive-is-not-overwritten
_why: spec §4. The skeleton drops apostrophes, so Mariana's measures 0.00 against the term Marianas — a perfect match — and the gate silently rewrote a correctly-transcribed word. 5 of 20 false applies in the English measurement; the guard took the shipping spotter 0.89 → 0.67 FP/1k.

name: spot-acoustic-ceiling-admits-strongly-heard-term
_why: spec §6. Herrakit → Parakeet is 0.625 string distance — well beyond the flat 0.45 ceiling — but was heard at −0.313, the best score of five terms. Acoustic evidence is doing work string similarity cannot see; 35 such detections were already found by the spotter and then discarded. Worth +4.7 points of end-to-end recall for zero additional false applies.

name: spot-acoustic-ceiling-is-conditional-not-flat
_why: spec §6: it MUST be conditional. A flat 0.65 admits 30 right and 25 wrong — two populations. At −2.0 (below the −1.8 floor, read off the strongest score among beyond-ceiling detections whose term was never spoken) the flat 0.45 holds and the same span is refused.

name: spot-acoustic-ceiling-ramps-between-anchors
_why: spec §6: −1.4 is the midpoint of the −1.8 → −1.0 ramp, so the ceiling is 0.55 and a 0.625 span is still refused. Pins the ramp itself, not just its two ends.

name: spot-non-acoustic-detection-keeps-flat-ceiling
_why: spec §6: the flag exists because `score` carries two incompatible scales. A detection that is NOT acoustic keeps 0.45 no matter how good its score looks — the model-free corrector's per-language distances are its own knob.

name: spot-possessive-term-still-applies
_why: the guard refuses to swap a possessive span for a NON-possessive term; a possessive term is untouched by it.

name: spot-multiword-not-placed-on-one-of-its-own-words
_why: NOT in the Windows spec — a third bug in the §2/§3 family, found while implementing §6 and reported upstream. 'claude' is 0.00 from the term's own first word and 0.40 from the whole term, so it is the first word correctly transcribed — 'Code' is simply not in the text. Publishing the term INSERTS a word: 'I love Claude Code wrote today'.

name: spot-multiword-partial-guard-holds-under-acoustic-ceiling
_why: the reason the partial-term guard could not wait: §6 widens the ceiling to 0.65 and code(4)/claudecode(10) is 0.60, so the acoustic ramp otherwise hands a bare 'code' the whole two-word term — 'I love load Claude Code today'.

name: spot-multiword-merged-token-still-applies
_why: the partial-term guard must NOT close the merged-token door — before §3 that was the only way a multi-word term ever landed. 'claudecode' is 0.00 from the whole term and 0.40 from 'claude', so the whole term wins and the apply stands.
